item.title: CoreStory: Building with AI in Systems You Don’t Fully Understand — Tue Aug 25, 2:00 PM
item.description:
Microsoft Reactor Toronto Most organizations aren't building on greenfield applications. They're building on decades of accumulated code, integrations, and undocumented business logic. As AI becomes a core part of software delivery, teams face a new challenge: how do humans and AI agents work effectively in systems nobody fully understands? This session explores the hidden costs of system ambiguity, compares common approaches to understanding legacy environments, and discusses how organizations can create a persistent intelligence layer with CoreStory that enables safer modernization, faster onboarding, and more confident AI-assisted development. Series Info - https://aka.ms/StartupSpotlight/S-1443 [EventID:27461]
Source: Meetup: Microsoft Reactor Toronto

item.title: Behind the Veil of the Frontier: AI Governance and the Developing World — Tue Aug 25, 6:00 PM — 30 Adelaide St E
item.description:
Address: 30 Adelaide St E Volunteers will escort you from the lobby up to the 12th floor. If you come late, you can call Georgia at 519 981 0360 Toronto, ON Canada
While developed nations enjoy proximity to frontier AI, discussions of AI in the developing world are often neglected.
How exactly does AI affect developing nations, and what is there to do about it? In this talk, Ashlyn Lu discusses stakeholders and perspectives of the Global South and emerging economies on frontier AI, as well as key vulnerabilities and possible solutions.
Hosted by Georgia Berg
Source: Luma Toronto Discover

item.title: The Toronto ML Systems Group: Diffusion Models — Tue Aug 25, 6:00 PM — Ideogram AI
item.description:
Address: Ideogram AI Toronto, ON Canada
Come hang out with The Toronto ML Systems Group. The theme for our fourth event is diffusion models. We’re bringing together people who care about the full stack behind modern AI, from chips and kernels to ML compilers, model architectures, attention variants, distributed training, inference optimization, and the hardware-software tradeoffs that shape what’s possible. This meetup is meant to be educational, recurring, and a little more conversational than formal, with enough structure to help you follow the whole stack without getting lost in the weeds. Whether you’re already working in ML…
Hosted by Melani Maheswaran & 3 others
Source: Luma Toronto Discover

item.title: Exit Points #75 — Fri Aug 28, 7:30 PM — Arraymusic
item.description:
Exit Points is a live music series that invites you into the world of musical improvisation, even if it’s your first time. Each event begins with simple listening strategies to help you feel more at ease with unfamiliar sounds and forms. You’ll then hear two short sets by small ensembles of expert musicians from a range of musical backgrounds, each exploring spontaneous and unscripted ways of making music together. The night ends with “Switchemups”: a fun, low-pressure session where audience members are welcome to join the musicians on stage and try improvising themselves (totally optional!). Expect an evening of surprising sounds, creative energy, and a warm, welcoming atmosphere.
Source: Toronto Events (Tockify)

item.title: An Unusual Zoroastrian Solution to the Problem of Evil — Fri Sep 11, 3:00 PM — Jackman Humanities Building
item.description: Speaker: Daniel Nolan (UC, Santa Cruz) The ‘Olamā-ye Eslām is a Zoroastrian apologetic work, perhaps from the thirteenth century CE. This paper argues that it contains a distinctive response to the problem of why an omnipotent and all-good deity would permit the existence of evil. Ormazd, the great good deity of Zoroastrianism, will not directly destroy or disable Ahriman, the chief source of all evil, because that would be incompatible with Ormazd’s perfect goodness. Instead, Ormazd is only permitted to achieve the neutralization of Ahriman through indirect means, wearing the author of evil out in a struggle for the material world. In focusing on which actions the good deity may perform, as opposed to the ends the good deity seeks, this theodicy takes an approach not found in contemporary discussions of the problem of evil.
